note: The golden set: twenty worksheets whose correct reading is known, so that
a change to a prompt or a model can be measured rather than argued about.
This file is the schema and the set in one. `target` is what a complete
set looks like; `worksheets` is what has actually been verified so far,
and `npm run eval` reports the shortfall rather than quietly measuring
against whatever happens to be here.
Every entry is hand-verified by a person who looked at the page. Nothing
in here is generated by a model, including the fields a model would be
good at guessing, because a golden set written by the thing it grades is
a mirror rather than a measurement.
A photograph goes in eval/photos/ and is named here by `photo`. An entry
with no photo is still useful: `printedText` alone exercises retrieval,
misconception matching and packet generation. Only the vision section
needs the image.
HOW THE SECTIONS USE IT
vision        needs `photo` and `extraction`
retrieval     needs `printedText` and `standardCode`
misconception needs `printedText`, `childWorkText` and `misconceptionId`
packet        needs `printedText` and `computedAnswer`
FIELDS
id               Short slug, unique in this file. Used in the verdict line.
photo            Filename in eval/photos/, or null for a text only entry.
grade            The year group the sheet was actually set for, or null
when the sheet does not say. Null is a real value here:
Child.grade is nullable and the pipeline infers the
grade from the retrieved standard, so a null entry is
testing the path an anonymous parent takes.
curriculum       'CCSS' for now. The field exists so that the England
National Curriculum and CBSE entries have somewhere to
go when those standards are sourced.
printedText      The printed question, transcribed by a person.
childWorkText    Everything the child wrote, one step per line, or null.
childAnswer      The child's final answer alone, or null.
computedAnswer   What mathjs should compute, as a string, or null where
the problem is not arithmetic mathjs can evaluate. This
is the string the packet section proves never appears in
the primer, the method comparison or the hint ladder.
standardCode     The one code a careful human would file this under.
standardAlso     Other codes that would also be correct. A retrieval that
lands here is a hit, not a miss.
misconceptionId  An id from seed/misconceptions.json, or null when the
working is correct, absent, or wrong in a way that is a
slip rather than a belief. Null is the commonest right
answer and the harness treats a model that invents a
match here as a failure, not a near miss.
note             Free text for a human. Never asserted.

worksheets.note: The worked exemplar. Every field filled, so a new entry can be copied from it. Matches seed/demo-packet.json, which is the fixture the product ships as its demo.
